title: Graceful cross-region handover for long-lived streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers using long-lived streaming sessions (WebSocket/HTTP2) experience abrupt disconnections and inconsistent token-level billing during cross-region failovers. Existing failover is optimized for short RPCs but causes either dropped streams or complex client-side retries that break session semantics.

Goal: Implement a server-side handover mechanism and coordinated routing policy to enable near-seamless active-active cross-region transitions for streaming sessions while preserving SLOs, preventing cascading overload, and enabling safe degradation paths. The solution must integrate with our routing layer, circuit breaker orchestration, and existing KV/prefix cache behaviors.

Non-goals: Transferring in-memory model KV cache between GPUs or live state migration of model-level caches is out of scope; we will rely on graceful fallbacks and short-lived resumptions instead of full state migration.
acceptance_criteria: New handover coordinator can initiate a planned switch of a streaming session from region A to region B with <3s median interruption for 95% of test sessions in staged canary.

Unplanned failover (region outage) leads to automatic controlled transition with documented degradation path: first attempt resume with reconnect token, then fallback to chunked non-streaming response if resume fails, within 10s for 90% of sessions.
No increase >5% in overall p99 end-to-end latency for non-stream (request/response) traffic during a canary handover window.
Circuit breaker policies prevent >10% additional load on destination region under overload scenarios; load-shedding decisions are logged and surfaced in Console for affected customers.
Telemetry dashboards show new metrics (handover_attempts, handover_success_rate, stream_resume_latency_ms, stream_degraded_count) and alerts when handover_success_rate < 95% for 10m.
Automated integration tests and a chaos experiment (region emulator) cover planned and unplanned handovers and are added to CI gating for gateway-2025.03 release.
Design doc and confluence runbook for on-call describing rollback and manual mitigation steps are published and reviewed by SRE and Platform leads.
design_decisions: Introduce a lightweight Handover Coordinator service colocated with edge gateways (stateless leader-elected per-pop) that issues a signed resume token to clients and target region.
Resume tokens are opaque, short-lived (TTL 30s), and contain session metadata pointers (session id, last acked offset, compression flags). Tokens do not contain model KV or secret material.

Client SDKs are extended to support a single transparent resume handshake: reconnect with Resume-Token header; server attempts delta-resume and continues stream. If resume fails, fallback to chunked response endpoint is invoked.

Traffic routing uses an orchestrated two-step shift: 1) warm-up (route a mirrored 1% of session reconnects to destination to populate routing and warm caches), 2) soft-shift (sticky hashing updated; handover coordinator signals token issuance), 3) cutover (routing change).

Circuit-breaker thresholds are derived from regional capacity signals (GPU queues, token throughput) and SLO headroom; on threshold breach destination region responds with 429+Retry-After and coordinator enacts progressive load-shedding rules (priority-based).
To preserve privacy/compliance we avoid sending raw request content during handover; only minimal metadata and offsets are used.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (lab): implement coordinator and resume token logic; unit and integration tests; local chaos tests.
Phase 2 (staged canary): enable for internal customers + 5 Beta tenants in us-west/us-east with 0.1% traffic mirrored to destination; verify telemetry and SLOs for 48h.
Phase 3 (regional): expand to 10% of streaming sessions across two region pairs; run 24h failover drills and circuit-breaker threshold tuning.
Phase 4 (global): default on for all hosted streaming sessions with opt-out via per-customer routing policy; monitor for 7 days before marking Done.
Kill switch: global feature flag at control plane to disable handover coordinator immediately; per-region fallback to existing failover behavior.
Post-rollout: Add an automated regression alert if stream_resume_latency_ms p95 exceeds 5s or handover_success_rate < 95% for any region pair.
telemetry_and_slos: Add metrics: handover_attempts, handover_successes, handover_failures, handover_median_resume_latency_ms, stream_resume_retries, stream_degraded_count, region_incoming_overload_events
SLO targets: initial release aims for handover_success_rate >= 95% and p95 resume latency < 5s. Non-stream SLO unaffected: 99.5% success within p99 < 200ms during canaries.
Alerting: fire when handover_success_rate < 90% for 5m OR stream_degraded_count increases > 50% vs baseline in 10m window.
Logs: emit structured events for each handover with fields: session_id, source_region, target_region, reason (planned|unplanned), resume_result, error_code, duration_ms.
Dashboards: ephemeral per-canary view and long-term aggregate; expose token-level billing impact delta during handovers.

qa_steps: Deploy coordinator to staging edge pair and enable canary flag for a small tenant.
Open 500 concurrent streaming sessions (mix of short and long-lived) and trigger a planned handover: verify resume tokens are issued and majority resume within 3s.
Simulate unplanned region outage via chaos emulator: validate automatic fallback path (resume attempts then chunked degrade) and ensure no more than 10% additional 429s on destination region.
Run load test on non-stream traffic during canary to ensure p99 latency delta < 5%.
Confirm structured logs and dashboard metrics appear; run alerting smoke tests.
